stories.headline: From Ronaldo to Ronaldinho: How these 10 footballers earned UAE Golden Visas and why
stories.deck: From Cristiano Ronaldo and Paul Pogba to Rio Ferdinand and Patrice Evra, several football legends have secured UAE Golden Visas and built connections with the region beyond the pitch. From business ventures and youth development to media careers and sports investments, explore how 10 footballers have used their long-term residency to expand their professional and personal ties with the Emirates.
stories.bodyText:
The UAE has spent years attracting some of football’s biggest names, but its Golden Visa programme offers more than a convenient way for global stars to visit the Emirates. Since the government expanded eligibility to exceptional sporting talent in 2020, footballers have used their connections with the country in different ways, from establishing businesses and investing in local football to building media ventures and developing opportunities for young players. Here are 10 footballers who received the coveted residency, and what their relationships with the UAE have looked like beyond the initial announcements.
What is the UAE Golden Visa, and why did footballers become eligible?
The UAE introduced its Golden Residency programme in 2019 under an initiative announced by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, the country’s Vice-President and Prime Minister and Dubai’s ruler. Initially associated with investors, entrepreneurs and specialised professionals, the programme offered eligible foreign nationals a longer-term alternative to conventional residence permits tied to employment or local sponsorship.
A significant expansion followed in 2020, when the UAE Cabinet extended the 10-year residency pathway to exceptional sporting talent. The Dubai Sports Council helped bring prominent international athletes into the programme, with 
Cristiano Ronaldo
 and several other football stars forming part of the first sporting cohort.
The change reflected an ambition extending beyond attracting famous visitors. Under the UAE’s economic diversification strategy, including the longer-term objectives associated with We the UAE 2031 and Dubai’s D33 Economic Agenda, global talent can help strengthen industries beyond oil, including technology, tourism, healthcare, education and professional sport.
Footballers offer a particularly visible connection between those ambitions and the wider public. Their international audiences can bring attention to local sporting facilities, youth development programmes, commercial partnerships and investment opportunities, while some recipients have gone on to establish more direct professional or business ties with the country.
What does the Golden Visa offer, and who can qualify?
The Golden Visa is a renewable, long-term residency permit that allows eligible foreign nationals to live, work, study and invest in the UAE without requiring an employer or another local sponsor to maintain their residency. Depending on the applicable category and eligibility conditions, the permit can last five or 10 years.
Its main benefits include:
- Long-term residency: Eligible holders receive renewable residency, providing greater continuity than shorter-term permits.
- Family sponsorship: Holders can sponsor spouses, children regardless of age and parents, alongside domestic workers under applicable regulations.
- Greater travel flexibility: Golden Visa holders can remain outside the UAE beyond the usual six-month absence limit that applies to many other residence visas.
- Professional independence: The residency arrangement does not depend on maintaining a conventional local employer sponsorship.
- Work, study and investment: Holders can pursue eligible professional, educational and commercial activities within the UAE.
- Entry arrangements for overseas applicants: Eligible applicants outside the country may receive a six-month multiple-entry visa, renewable for another six months, to complete residency procedures.
Following the expansion, the programme now covers several categories, including property investors, entrepreneurs, scientists, skilled professionals, outstanding students and graduates, humanitarian pioneers, and exceptional talents in sport, culture and the arts. Each pathway has its own criteria and application or nomination process, so receiving the visa does not necessarily require buying property or taking up employment with a UAE-based organisation.
For footballers, the expanded sporting category created a route to long-term residency based on exceptional achievement and talent, rather than requiring them to leave their existing clubs and move to the Emirates.
Ten footballers who received the UAE Golden Visa
1. Cristiano Ronaldo (February 2020)
Portuguese forward Cristiano Ronaldo received his 10-year UAE Golden Visa in February 2020 while playing for Juventus, becoming one of the most prominent beneficiaries of the newly expanded sporting category. The recognition followed his sixth Best Men's Player accolade at the Dubai Globe Soccer Awards on 29 December 2019, reflecting both his international standing and his established relationship with the Emirate.
His placement in the inaugural sporting cohort demonstrated that an athlete could maintain an active career abroad while holding long-term UAE residency. Ronaldo subsequently signed with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia in January 2023, extending his commitment through June 2027, while frequently visiting Dubai for personal and professional obligations. To anchor this long-term connection to the region, Ronaldo expanded his international real estate portfolio by acquiring a €25 million plot of land on Jumeirah Bay Island—a highly exclusive, seahorse-shaped enclave widely known as "Billionaire Island". The acquisition was made to construct a custom waterfront mega-mansion, providing a permanent family base in the UAE just a short distance from his football commitments in Riyadh.
Al Nassr's Cristiano Ronaldo celebrates their first goal, scored by Angelo. (Reuters Photo)
His relationship with the Emirates also features a prominent personal dimension, highlighted by a well-documented friendship with the Crown Prince of Dubai, Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum. Ronaldo has repeatedly spoken warmly of the city, stating during an appearance at Expo 2020 Dubai on 28 January 2022: “I thank all my fans... I love Dubai, its culture and its people, and I visit Dubai every year, and I am very happy to be here.”
2. Didier Drogba  (November 2020)
Former Chelsea and Ivory Coast striker Didier Drogba received his Golden Visa in November 2020, when Major General Mohammad Ahmad Al Marri, director of Dubai’s General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs, welcomed him at the department’s headquarters to present the residency card.
The recognition came after a decorated career that included four English Premier League titles and a Champions League crown with Chelsea. Drogba was also presented with the 
Medal of First Line of Defence
 in appreciation of his support for the Dubai Sports Council’s 
Be Fit, Be Safe
 campaign, which encouraged residents to prioritise physical wellbeing during the pandemic.
Football Legend Didier Drogba, attends the E1 powerboat Grand Prix Championship race in Lagos, Nigeria, Sunday, Oct. 5, 2025. (AP Photo/Sunday Alamba)
His connection with Dubai extended beyond football, with the former striker exploring opportunities involving commercial property, sports academies and the wider sports sector. He has also participated in international business events, including AIBC Eurasia, bringing his sporting profile into discussions around emerging technology, blockchain and investment.
3. Ronaldinho (May 2021)
Brazilian World Cup winner Ronaldinho, whose full name is Ronaldo de Assis Moreira, received his 10-year Golden Visa in May 2021 through Dubai’s General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs. Major General Mohammed Al Marri and his deputy, Major General Obaid Muhair bin Surour, were present when the former Barcelona and AC Milan playmaker received the residency.
Ronaldinho’s relationship with the UAE has included ambitions around youth football and wider sporting partnerships. He signed a strategic memorandum of understanding with Abu Dhabi-based Palms Sports, establishing a framework intended to combine elite athletic development with academic opportunities for young Emirati athletes.
He has also laid the groundwork for a 
Ronaldinho Football Academy
 in Dubai, with the proposed project centred on structured coaching and the Brazilian approach to attacking football commonly associated with 
Joga Bonito
. His wider appearances across the region have included sports events, corporate gatherings and digital-technology exhibitions, where his global profile attracts audiences beyond traditional football supporters.
Ronaldinho has regularly visited and trained in Dubai since his youth, making the city a familiar base for his regional engagements. His Golden Visa provides long-term residency flexibility while he explores sporting, commercial and cultural opportunities across the Emirates.
4. Paul Pogba (February 2020)
French midfielder and World Cup winner Paul Pogba was among the elite sporting figures granted a UAE Golden Visa in February 2020. At the time, the former Manchester United star had already established a strong connection with Dubai, regularly utilizing the city's sports infrastructure for off-season conditioning and warm-weather training.
Dubai’s high-performance training centres have been central to Pogba’s conditioning and rehabilitation, particularly at Nad Al Sheba Sports Complex and Transform Altitude Performance Center. He has also supported local fitness campaigns with the Dubai Sports Council and mentored young players at community events.
Soccer Football - Ligue 1 - AS Monaco v Olympique de Marseille - Stade Louis II, Monaco - April 5, 2026 AS Monaco's Paul Pogba inside the stadium before the match REUTERS/Manon Cruz
His regional interests have since expanded beyond football into traditional Gulf sports culture. In late 2025, Pogba became a significant shareholder and global ambassador for Al Haboob, the world’s first professional camel racing team. The Saudi-founded organization competes heavily across the UAE and the wider Gulf region, aiming to modernize the sport by introducing advanced sports science, data tracking, and robotic jockey technology. Pogba’s involvement is intended to help elevate camel racing to a global audience, bridging the gap between historical heritage and modern professional sports management.
5. Romelu Lukaku (February 2020)
Belgian striker Romelu Lukaku was another big name from that initial wave of sports stars to secure a UAE Golden Visa in February 2020, right while he was dominating Serie A with Inter Milan. The long-term residency was a massive nod to his status as one of Europe’s top forwards, giving him a permanent tie to the Emirates without having to uproot his club career.
Lukaku’s Dubai connection grew at the 14th Dubai International Sports Conference, where he joined João Félix and Mikael Silvestre to discuss football technology. He also spoke about coping with online racism, urging young players to use social media positively. The event ended with a viral moment when a UAE royal presented him with a golden plaque that misspelled his name as “Romello”.
Soccer Football - Nations League - Group A1 - Belgium v Turkey - Stade Maurice Dufrasne, Liege, Belgium - October 2, 2026 Belgium's Romelu Lukaku celebrates scoring their third goal REUTERS/Yves Herman
When he isn’t speaking at summits, Lukaku uses Dubai as his ultimate reset button. He’s a regular at the world-class Nad Al Sheba Sports Complex during league winter breaks, using the warm weather and high-tech facilities to keep his conditioning at an elite level. His routine fits perfectly into Dubai's push to become the global capital for off-season athletic recovery.
6. Luís Figo (February 2020)
Former Portugal international Luís Figo, the 2000 Ballon d’Or winner who played for Barcelona, Real Madrid and Inter Milan, received his Golden Visa as part of the February 2020 sporting initiative. The residency recognised his career at the highest level while giving him a long-term base for professional and commercial activities across the region.
Figo has maintained links with Dubai through brand partnerships and sporting events, including collaborations with Mastercard Middle East and Africa during Expo 2020 Dubai. His appearances included fan meet-and-greet sessions and promotional activities featuring the UEFA Champions League trophy.
Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - Group A - Mexico v South Africa - Estadio Azteca, Mexico City, Mexico - June 11, 2026 Former player Luis Figo poses for a picture as he arrives before the match REUTERS/Eloisa Sanchez
He also participated in a Guinness World Record initiative involving the highest-altitude football match played on a parabolic flight, a campaign coordinated through Dubai. Alongside those commercial engagements, Figo supported the Dubai Sports Council’s Be Fit, Be Safe campaign during the pandemic, encouraging residents to remain physically active while public spaces were restricted.
His post-playing career has increasingly involved ambassadorial work and international business events, making the Golden Visa a useful foundation for maintaining commitments across Europe and the Middle East.
7. Roberto Carlos  (February 2020)
Brazilian World Cup winner and former Real Madrid left-back Roberto Carlos received his Golden Visa in February 2020, joining a group of football legends recognised for their sporting achievements and connections with the Emirates. His relationship with Dubai has included exhibition matches, community fitness initiatives and youth football development.
In August 2026, Carlos became a co-owner and shareholder of Dubai-based Fursan Hispania FC, alongside former footballers Michel Salgado and Fernando Hierro. The club’s youth development ambitions offer him a more direct role in the local game, using international football connections and technical experience to help develop young players and create pathways towards professional opportunities in Europe.
Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - Final - Spain v Argentina - VIP Arrivals - New York New Jersey Stadium, East Rutherford, New Jersey, U.S. - July 19, 2026 Former Brazil player Roberto Carlos arrives at the stadium ahead of the match REUTERS/Amanda Perobelli
Carlos has also supported the Real Madrid Foundation’s work in the UAE through a partnership with ISD Sports City, helping launch an educational football programme at the ISD La Liga Academy campus. The initiative provides training for more than 1,000 young footballers.
His work also includes youth clinics and appearances promoting Real Madrid World at Dubai Parks and Resorts, extending his involvement from football development into the UAE’s sports tourism sector.
8. Miralem Pjanić (February 2020)
Bosnian midfielder Miralem Pjanić received his Golden Visa in February 2020 while playing for Juventus, becoming one of the active European footballers included in the programme’s first sporting cohort. His subsequent career gave him a particularly direct connection with the Emirates when he left Barcelona in September 2022 to join Sharjah FC.
Unlike recipients whose UAE relationships have centred mainly on visits and commercial appearances, Pjanić played in the UAE Pro League for two seasons between 2022 and 2024. His experience at Juventus and Barcelona brought elite European experience into the domestic competition, and he helped Sharjah win the UAE President’s Cup and the UAE League Cup.
During his time in the country, Pjanić also had opportunities to mentor younger domestic players, sharing experience from years competing at the highest levels of European football. Following his UAE spell and later playing career, he maintained ties with Dubai and became involved with Mundial Football Academy, a venture focused on identifying and training grassroots talent using high-performance football methods.
9. Rio Ferdinand (2021)
Former Manchester United and England captain Rio Ferdinand transitioned to a permanent life in the UAE in August 2025, relocating his family to a £6.5 million mansion in Dubai's luxury Al Barari community. This move followed his departure from his prominent UK punditry role at TNT Sports in May 2025. While he enjoyed a long-standing relationship with the region, this relocation marked the formal establishment of Dubai as the central base for his media work, business interests, and 10-year UAE Golden Visa residency framework.
Soccer Football - Saudi Pro League - Al Nassr v Al Ahli - Al Awwal Park, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia - April 29, 2026 Al Nassr's Cristiano Ronaldo with former footballer and TV pundit Rio Ferdinand before the match REUTERS/Stringer
Ferdinand has since actively scaled his digital media platform, Rio Presents, while anchoring himself in the UAE’s expanding creator economy. He was featured as a prominent fireside speaker at Dubai’s 1 Billion Followers Summit, where he discussed the future of digital media and how modern creators can build sustainable international audiences independently of traditional television.
Beyond media, his regional business activities extend into real estate through strategic partnerships with prominent firms like LEOS Developments. In the sports and tourism sector, he co-operates Football Escapes, a premium holiday football coaching concept that organizes youth camps led by UEFA-licensed former professionals at luxury resorts.
Ferdinand and his wife, Kate, also engage with the local community through public wellness initiatives, including fitness events hosted at Jumeirah Beach near the Burj Al Arab.
10. Patrice Evra (2021)
Former Manchester United champion and French national team captain Patrice Evra was awarded his UAE Golden Visa back in 2021 under the exceptional-talent framework. . Since then, he has fully leaned into the local lifestyle, famously calling Dubai his "home sweet home" and basing himself out of a luxury penthouse on the Palm Jumeirah.
Instead of just enjoying retirement, Evra has used his long-term visa to pivot into a serious second career as a Dubai-based entrepreneur. He has set up several companies in the UAE covering everything from beauty and fitness to deep tech. In fact, while speaking at regional business events like the Invest in Sharjah forum and Token2049 Dubai, he pointed out just how much of a game-changer the region's geography is for a global business. He noted that with nearly two-thirds of the world’s population sitting within an eight-hour flight, running a global empire from Dubai feels a world away from his old days managing companies in the UK, where he felt entirely isolated from fast-growing markets like Asia.
Patrice Evra. Image by Jonathan Moscrop / PA
Lately, Evra has been bridging the gap between real estate and sports technology. He officially partnered with UAE developer Major Developments as a core project partner for Colibri Views, a massive new high-rise project at RAK Central in Ras Al Khaimah. Evra actually designed the crown jewel of the tower himself: the UAE's very first rooftop Footbot simulator. It’s an AI-driven, high-tech football arena packed with smart motion sensors and performance tracking to help residents train like elite pros.
On top of the commercial tech, he is also focused on grassroots football through his Dubai-based project, Love This Game FC. The whole idea is to scout and train young local talent in the UAE, giving them a real pathway to score professional trials over in Europe and the UK.

briefs.headline: Rohan Bopanna returns to action, will represent Gurgaon Grand Slammers in TPL
briefs.deck: Argentina's world No. 60 Roman Burruchaga, representing the Kolkata Thunder Blades, will be the highest-ranked singles player in the league
briefs.bodyText:
Former world No. 1 Rohan Bopanna and 2023 Australian Open men's doubles winner Rinky Hijikata were on Tuesday (October 6, 2026) revealed as marquee players of their respective teams at the Tennis Premier League (TPL) ahead of the player auction on October 12 in Mumbai.
Bopanna will represent Gurgaon Grand Slammers.
"Every year, the league gets stronger, and I love the team environment and energy the format brings. This year, the competition will be very high, with a great mix of experienced players and young Indian talent," said Bopanna.
Argentina's world No. 60 Roman Burruchaga, representing the Kolkata Thunder Blades, will be the highest-ranked singles player in the league.
Hijikata, who will represent the Rajasthan Rangers, has already tasted Grand Slam success. He also reached the 2025 Wimbledon men's doubles final and achieved a career-high doubles ranking of world No. 23.
"I'm really excited to be part of the Rajasthan Rangers and make my Kia TPL debut this season. The 25-point format makes the league very exciting, and I’m looking forward to experience the energy in Hyderabad."
Frenchman Terence Atmane, nicknamed "The Magician", will headline the Mumbai Royals.
The Lucknow Blazers will be represented by Czechia’s Dalibor Svrcina, who returns for a second consecutive season with the same team.
Croatia's Dino Prizmic will be the marquee player for the Hyderabad Strikers. A former junior world No. 1 and the 2023 Roland Garros boys’ singles champion, the 21-year-old reached a career-high ranking of world No. 70 this year.
Representing the defending champions, GS Delhi Aces, will be Australian Adam Walton, who has achieved a career-high ranking of world No. 74 and brings extensive ATP Tour and Grand Slam experience to the Delhi team.
Completing the eight-player marquee line-up will be Frenchman Alexandre Muller, who will represent the Gujarat Panthers once again this season.
One of the most experienced players in the line-up, the 29-year-old has achieved a career-high ranking of world No. 38.
The matches during the TPL Season 8 will be held from December 8-13.

briefs.headline: Committee formed to ensure HIL’s continuation
briefs.bodyText:
The Sports Ministry has constituted a seven-member committee to work out the modalities of the governance structure and way forward to ensure the continuation of the Hockey India League.
Headed by former Odisha sports secretary and currently joint secretary (Khelo India) R. Vineel Krishna as the government’s representative, the committee includes Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey, secretary general Bholanath Singh and treasurer Sekar J. Manoharan among others. The three representatives named from among the HIL franchises are JSW Sports CEO Divyanshu Singh, SG Pipers’ CEO Mahesh Bhupathi and Hyderabad Toofans’ owner Alok Sanghi.
The ministry had directed formation of a committee to find a resolution to the stalemate and uncertainty surrounding the HIL and working out the governance and financial models for the league. The move comes amidst growing friction between Tirkey and other HI officials including Bholanath with the latter reportedly calling two consecutive executive board meetings despite Tirkey’s declaring them as illegal and invalid.
Meanwhile, sources claimed that the IOA’s committee constituted to look into allegations of harassment by former captain Asunta Lakra had its first meeting on Wednesday. Interestingly Mamta Kharab, the one former hockey player nominated in the committee, was not part of Wednesday’s hearing.
Elections deferred
The Hockey India elections, initially scheduled for November 7, have been postponed with fresh dates yet to be announced. Sources said the elections might now take place by the end of next month or early December, citing HI rules that mandate a 60-day notice and the unavailability of the appointed electoral officer Sudhir Tripathi.
The decision was taken in the HI EB meeting held here on Tuesday. Interestingly, it has also been learnt that Tirkey has filed a petition in the Delhi High Court against the federation’s two most recent EB meetings and the decisions taken therein, including the pending elections.

briefs.headline: India must stay alert for 90 minutes: Jamil
briefs.deck: ‘We were okay in the first 30 minutes; after that, maybe it was fitness, maybe concentration, the lack of which contributed to the loss,’ said Khalid Jamil
briefs.bodyText:
The Indian men’s football team ended its three-match FIFA international friendly window on a disappointing note, suffering a 1-6 defeat against Uruguay at the Salt Lake Stadium on Tuesday (October 6, 2026). However, head coach Khalid Jamil’s post-match assessment focused less on the heavy defeat and more on the lack of concentration that contributed to India’s defensive lapses.
Also read | India’s fight fades as Uruguay nets six
Jamil repeatedly highlighted the need for the players to remain focused throughout the match as India played its matches against Panama, Brazil and Uruguay. Much like what it did against Panama and Brazil, India showed encouraging signs against Uruguay, attempting to press high and attack despite facing a team considerably higher in the FIFA rankings. But Jamil felt those positive spells meant little when defensive mistakes were punished.
“The key thing is that one mistake in a good game can be punished,” Jamil said, stressing the need for his players to remain sharp and alert throughout the match.
India was competitive during the opening half-hour but struggled to maintain that level thereafter.
“We were okay in the first 30 minutes. After that, maybe it was fitness, maybe concentration, the lack of which contributed to the loss. That is why we have to be more alert because we conceded more goals around the 60th and 70th minutes,” Jamil analysed.
Jamil also underlined the importance of preparation and collective responsibility. “Your preparation has to be good, and your concentration has to remain strong both before and during the game. There can be no distractions. At this level, even if you play a good game, one mistake can be punished,” he said.
The three friendlies have offered India both encouragement and a warning. India showed it can compete against stronger opponents in patches, but must turn those spells into sustained performances. With the New Zealand test due next in November, Jamil will look to build a more disciplined, resilient and switched-on side capable of competing for the full 90 minutes.
Uruguay coach Diego Forlan said his side recovered well after India made a positive start. “Our transition and our passing was a little bit slow at the start, so India could profit from that. Then, we tried to fix it, and as the game progressed, we controlled the pressing really well,” the former Uruguay star forward now working as the team’s interim coach said about his side’s performance.

briefs.headline: CRICKET | History will be kinder to you: Gambhir to Agarkar
briefs.bodyText:
A day after the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) invited applications for his successor, Ajit Agarkar was publicly thanked for his three-year stint as chairman of the men’s selection committee, with head coach Gautam Gambhir acknowledging the former India fast bowler’s contribution to a period of considerable success.
“Dear Ajit Bhai, an absolute honour to work with you,” Gambhir wrote on X on Tuesday morning. “Those 3 ICC trophies are testimony of your conviction: Team first & Team ahead, always. I must say, History will be kinder to you. Thank you for everything.”
The BCCI followed it up in the evening with a tribute to Agarkar, highlighting the trophies won during his tenure, including three ICC titles and two Asia Cup triumphs, as well as back-to-back Asian Games gold medals and India’s run to the 2023 ODI World Cup final.
“Thank you, Mr Ajit Agarkar, for your commitment, conviction and contribution as Chairman of the Men’s Selection Committee,” the board said.
Agarkar took over as chairman in July 2023 and was handed a renewed contract before his tenure expired on October 4. The BCCI’s farewell messages came a day after it formally opened the process for appointing his replacement.
His tenure encompassed some significant selection calls, as India transitioned across formats while collecting major silverware. The three ICC trophies referenced by Gambhir include the 2024 T20 World Cup, the 2025 Champions Trophy and the 2026 T20 World Cup.
Agarkar’s departure leaves a four-member selection committee, with Pragyan Ojha currently chairing it on an interim basis.

briefs.headline: IND u-19 vs AUS u-19 | Baloda scalps a record-breaking 14 in India u-19’s dominant win
briefs.deck: The hosts bowl out Australia under-19 for 151 to set up an 11-run chase; Cattle’s lone battle only delays the inevitable as Yashbardhan & Co. clinch the series 2-0
briefs.bodyText:
Tanmay Baloda recorded the best-ever match figures in a youth ‘Test’ (14 for 73) to help India under-19 register a thumping 10-wicket win over Australia under-19 at the Narendra Modi Stadium here on Wednesday.
The hosts bowled out the visitors for 151, with Baloda scalping eight for 41 in the second innings. Asked to chase a mere 11 runs, India u-19 finished the game in five deliveries.
At the start of day three, Australia u-19 was at 86 for four, 55 runs in the red.
Baloda began his morning with a wicket off his first ball. Continuing his modus operandi, he pitched the ball on stumps and trapped Zed Hollick in front while the batter was on the defensive. He cleaned up Charlie Henderson in his next over with a quicker one.
Pacer Priyanshu Singh got one to cut into Jacob Pietz and uproot the off stump before pinning Thomas Vaseo.
Cattle showed immense maturity and farmed the strike with No. 10 Patrick Sullivan at the other end. Skipper Yashbardhan Chauhan kept the field open to prevent Cattle from targeting the fence, forcing the batter to take singles.
Sullivan supported Cattle for a while, but Baloda eventually had the former caught at first slip.
Cattle came down the track and sent Ayaan Akram’s delivery over long-off to reach his half-century. He then moved his front leg to clear the long-on boundary, taking Australia past India’s mark.
However, Cattle was eventually bowled while trying to take on Baloda as India u-19 went on to sweep the multi-day series 2-0.

briefs.headline: Dhir’s impact with the ball was decisive in the first T20I
briefs.bodyText:
Three weeks ago, Naman Dhir was with the Punjab team preparing for the Ranji Trophy campaign when he learned he had been selected for the India ODI squad. After playing all three matches in the 50-over format, Dhir was added to the T20 squad in the eleventh hour, making it a dream fortnight.
On Tuesday, the all-rounder made his first real mark in international cricket, albeit in a facet of his game few have seen.
“It was a great feeling when I got the call. I was in the Ranji Trophy camp at the PCA. Right away I called my father; he was emotional; I also got a little emotional,” said Dhir.
“Obviously, every kid has a dream to play for the country, so if you represent the country, it’s a big deal. I am from a small town and no one had played for the country from there. So it’s a big deal for me and in our area.”
Match-ups and analytics have meant captains are reluctant to trust finger spinners, especially off-spinners, in T20s. Operating as the fifth bowling option, Dhir’s figures of three for 31 on his T20 debut played a key role in India’s eight-wicket win over West Indies here.
The most impressive aspect of his bowling was how he responded to being attacked, showing real smarts and temperament. Every time he was hit, the 26-year-old adjusted, whether by bowling it wide outside off-stump, slowing it up, or altering his length to induce false shots. Remarkably, all his wicket-taking deliveries came just after he was hit for a six.
“I saw Axar (Patel) bhai in the PowerPlay, where he was bowling a little slow. It was turning. I thought if I slow it down, with the wicket gripping, I can get them out. So I just stuck to my basic plan and got good results,” he added.
While he has made his name through his batting in the IPL for Mumbai Indians, Dhir revealed that he has always worked on his bowling. “I’ve been bowling for a long time. It’s not like I’ve just started. In IPL, yes, there’s an Impact Player rule, so you see me bowling less. But it’s not like I haven’t bowled; I’ve bowled a lot and got wickets.”
“I hope I’ll keep doing well in the future,” said Dhir.
